headline: Agentic high-level synthesis with RTL refinement reports faster FPGA kernels than direct RTL on a bounded benchmark
summary: The authors compare agents designing FPGA kernels directly in RTL with workflows that use high-level synthesis (HLS) and post-HLS RTL refinement. On an 11-task benchmark, they report a 2.62× geometric-mean speedup in simulated execution time for agent-based HLS with RTL refinement over direct RTL across 13 valid task/model pairs; agent-based HLS alone reports 2.31× across 15 valid pairs. The experiments use Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.6 Sol in the same pi harness, AMD Alveo U55C and Vitis 2025.2, with each experiment run once. The metric combines simulated cycle count with the greater of post-route clock period or target period. These are paper-reported FPGA results, not an independent reproduction, production ASIC benchmark or measured cost reduction.
